items.title: The Power Brokers
items.description: My first investigation: how power really gets negotiated, from council chambers to the corridors of influence. A beginner's course in documents, sources and patience.

items.title: Broken Chains
items.description: Early reporting practice on global trade: following the money through supply chains, and learning to make a complex story clear for everyday readers.

items.title: The Women Rewriting Energy
items.description: An interview series in progress: conversations with the people building the renewable future, practising the craft of listening first and asking sharper questions second.

items.title: The Librarian of the Last Archive
items.description: A profile practice piece: the archivist fighting digital amnesia. A reminder that every story starts with someone worth listening to.

items.title: The Housing Divide
items.description: Campus and community reporting on housing: telling a policy story through the people who live it, one interview at a time.

items.title: Skyline of Opportunity
items.description: International correspondence in training: reporting on how fast-growing cities are reshaping the world, with the ambition of someone determined to get there.

items.title: The Ink Is Dry
items.description: My first essay on the future of journalism — a student's love letter to print in a digital age, and a first attempt at a strong, fair argument.

items.title: The Price of Progress
items.description: Opinion writing practice on technology and its human cost — learning to make a case in 800 words without losing the nuance.

items.title: Faces of the City
items.description: My photography practice in progress: documenting the workers and places the headlines forget, and learning to tell stories with light and composition.

items.title: Reel & Real
items.description: A first multimedia experiment: short video storytelling, discovering how the journalist's craft grows beyond the written word.
